canonical_question: Did the ultrasonic cleaning in isopropanol leave any residual organic contaminants that could affect the initial mass measurement?

question_variants.question: Did the ultrasonic cleaning in isopropanol leave any residual organic contaminants that could affect the initial mass measurement?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The document mentions ultrasonic cleaning in isopropanol but does not report results or analysis regarding residual organic contaminants.

answers.answer: The text states specimens were ultrasonically cleaned in isopropanol, but provides no evidence regarding the efficacy of this step in removing organics or the presence of residual contaminants affecting mass measurements.
answers.boundary_limitation: No post-cleaning surface analysis or mass baseline verification regarding organics is provided.
evidence_spans: Figure 1 a shows the XRD pattern of the AlNbTiVZr 0.25 alloy in the initial (annealed at 1200 °C for 24 h) condition.

In the XRD pattern, the Bragg peaks belonging to two phases, namely B2 and Zr 5 Al 3 , were found; the lattice parameters of B2 and Zr 5 Al 3 phases were a = 0.3203 nm and a = 0.7996 nm, c = 0.5374 nm, respectively.

The alloy consisted of two structural constituents: (i) B2 grains (labeled with 1 in Figure 1 b) with the average size of ~80 μm and the chemical composition close to that of the alloy ( Table 1 ) and (ii) light-grey (Zr, Al)-rich particles (labeled with 2 in Figure 1 b; Table 1 ) identified as the Zr 5 Al 3 phase located both along the boundaries of the B2 grains as a discontinuous network and as separate particles or clusters of these particles in the B2 grains interior.
